prompt: At 7 p.m. there were 6.5 inches of snow on the ground at Nina's house. Snow fell at 0.8 inches per hour until 10 p.m., and then it stopped. Starting at 9 a.m. the next morning, the snow melted at 0.3 inch per hour. How many inches deep was the snow at 4 p.m.?
explanation: From 7 p.m. to 10 p.m. is 3 hours, so 0.8 x 3 = 2.4 inches fell, and the depth reached 6.5 + 2.4 = 8.9 inches. From 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. is 7 hours, so 0.3 x 7 = 2.1 inches melted. 8.9 - 2.1 = 6.8 inches.
quantity_asked: the depth of the snow at the final time, in inches

subskill: Minutes to knit a length from a gauge (rows per inches) and a time per row
grade_rationale: High for grade 6 (6.RP.A.3): a ratio (rows per inches) scaled to a length, then a time per row and a seconds-to-minutes conversion.
prompt: A knitting pattern has 18 rows for every 4 inches of length. Ella's headband will be 10 inches long, and each row takes Ella 35 seconds to knit. How many minutes will it take Ella to knit the headband?
